RECORDS.

THURSDAY, MAY 6, 1897.

The Couvention in the sixty-fourth year of the
Fraternity, with the Xi
Chapter in Wesleyau University, at Middletown, Conn., was called to order,
at 10.30 A. M., in the Xi Chapter Hall,
by Bro. Herbert L. Bridgman
{F '66), of the Executive Council, who named Bro. L. K. Willman (3 '97)
Temporary President, and Bro. R. D. Whiting {3 '98) Temporary Recorder.
Bro. J. 8. Judd (3 '85), Chairman of the Committee of
Arrangements, in
brief remarks, welcomed the delegates to the home of the
Xi, and the follow
ing committees were announced by the Temporary President :
On Pbrmaitent Organization. Bros. John Gowdy (3 '97), R. A. With
erspoon (r '97) and L. Horton (M '97).
On Chedentials. Bros. E. W. WaUin {A '97), Robert W. Carle
{B '97)
and F. P. Sackett {2 '97).
After a recess of twenty minutes the Committee on Permanent
Organiza
tion reported the following as permanent officers :

President.
H. L. Bbidgman {F '66).

Vice-Presidents.
Francis S. Bangs {A '78),
George S. Colp:man (3 '76),
George C. Howland {F '85).

Recorder.
W. G. GiEPiN (3 '97).

Assistant Recorders.
H. R. Remsen (3 '98),
R. W. Abbott {A '98).

The Committee on Credentials reported ths following list of duly
accredited
Delegates.

Coleman (3 '76).

The report was accepted and the Convention having
unanimously adopted
the rules of the Convention of 1893, the Annual Communication of the Exec
utive Council (see pages 10-13) was presented by Secretary Bro.
Bangs.
A recess of half an hour was ordered, in order that the representatives of
the St. Stephen's College petitioners might be heard. The delegates and others
assembled in the reception room on the lower floor of the Xi Chapter
House,
Bro. George C. Howland presiding, and were addressed by Rev. Dr. F. S.
Archdeacon of
Sill^
Albany, N. Y., and Rev. G. S. Bennett, of Jersey City, in
support of the petition from the Eulexian Society, and Mr. J. B. Greiner in
support of that from the Kappa Gamma Chi.
Upon the re-assembling of the Convention, the Committee on Credentials
reported the presence of the delegates, Bros. W. N. Kennedy ('93) and P. B.
Stanberry ('98), of the lota.
The following Standing Committees were announced
by the President :
To Nominate an Executive Council : Bros. Louis Diven
{H '97) F P
Sackett {2 '97), Vrooman Mason (P '95), Eugene W.
Murry (iT '98) and
Edgar G. Pratt {K '97).

5

On the Annual Communication : Bros. John
Gowdy (S* '97), Owen J.
Roberts {T '95), F. P. Keppel, Jr. (^'98), Edward
Sawyer (B '98) and John
B. Keating, (#'98).
On Unfinished Business : Bros. W. E. Merriman, Jr.
(0 '98), Richard
Marcy (.^'98), P. D. Briggs {W '98), L. E. Horton (M '97) and P. B. Stan-
berry, Jr. {I '98).
On New Business: Bros. Charles H. Blair, Jr. (X
'97), P. H. Boynton
{F '97), David Orr {A '97), George S. McCook {BB '97) and Robert A. Wither
spoon {T '97).
The President reported the reference of the Annual Communication
(Ap
pendix A, pages 10 13), the Table of Membership (Appendix B, page 13) and
the Treasurer's Report (Appendix C, pages 14 and 15) to the Committee on
the Annual Communication, and the petitions from the Omega Club in Chicago

University (Appendix D, pages 16-18) and the Kulexian and Kappa Gamma
Chi Societies of St. Stephen's College (Appendix E, pages 19 and 30) to the
Committee on New Business.
Recess.

The Committee to nominate an Executive Council nominated as members
of the Council for the ensuing year Bros. Herbert L. Bridgman (F '66),
Francis 8. Bangs {A '78), WiUiam M. Kingsley {A '83), Frank L. Hall {B '73),
George S. Coleman (3 '76), who were, thereupon, unanimously elected, VicePresident Howland in the chair.
The Committee on the Ammal Communication presented General Resolu
tions Nos. 1-6(see page 7), which were, under suspension of the rules, unani
mously adopted.
The same Committee also presented General Resolution No. 7 (see page
7). During the discussion which followed, upon the request of Bro. Charles
W. Smiley {^ '74), the stipulation tendered to the graduate members of the
Cmega Chapter, under General Resolution No. 11, of 1896, and the correspon
dence in relation thereto (Appendix F, pages 31-33), were read in full. The
resolution was adopted by unanimous vote.
The Committee also presented General Resolution No. 8 (see page 7),
which was adopted unanimouslj', the Psi not voting.
The Committee also presented Special Resolution No. 1, which was unani
mously adopted.
The Committee also presented General Resolution No. 9, as follows :
"
That the application for the establishment of a Chapter at the University
of Chicago be granted without specification as to the Chapter name, and that
action upon the question be immediately taken by the several Chapters of the
Fraternity." Discussion ensuing, at the close of the debate, the resolution as
reported by the Committee was adopted by the following vote :

6

Ate 

Theta, Delta, Beta, Sigma, Gamma, Zeta, Lambda, Kappa, Psi, Xi,
Upsilon, Pi, Chi,. Beta Beta 14.
Nat Iota, Phi, Eta, Tau, Mu and Rho 6.
President Rev. Dr. George E. Reed (t' '69), of Dickinson College at Car
lisle. Pa., being present, upon invitation of the chair, briefly addressed the
Convention upon the general welfare and prosperity of the Fraternity, and
the Recorder read the following telegram from the Pi :
"
Syracuse, N. Y At 8.30 this morning ground was broken for the new

Chapter House.
Theodore L. Waugh."

Adjourned until Friday morning at 10 o'clock.

FRIDAY, MAY 7, 1897.
The minutes of the previous sessions having been read and
approved, the
Committee on New Business presented General Resolution No. 10
(see
page 7).
The Secretary of the Council presented a statement
(Appendix G, page 34)
showing the places at which the Conventions of the last twenty-five years had
been held. Bro. Adams (iT) stated that it was the
hope of his Chapter to
hold the Convention in its new house in 1900, and the resolution was then
adopted.
The Committee on New Business presented Resolution No.
11, as follows :
General Resolution No. 11. Resolved, That the Executive
Council be re
quested to investigate the matter of a standard pin, an authorized ieweler and
a uniform place of a full of
wearing, report the same to be submitted to the
Convention next year.

Bro. Bangs called the attention of the Convention to the
report by the
Council to the Convention of '96, showing the
adoption
of a uniform badge
and the resolution was, ou motion of Bro.
Boynton {F), amended and adopted
(see page 8).
The Committee also reported Special Resolution No.
3. After an appreci
ative tribute by Bro. Isaac F. Russell
{A '75) to the memory and character
of Bro. Bayliss, the resolution was
adopted.
Bro. Howland, by unanimous consent, addressed
the Convention the
upon
Chicago-Omega matter, after which Bro. Bangs offered General Resolution
No. 13. The rules having been suspended,
upon roll call, the resolution was
unanimously adopted.
Upon motion of Bro. Howland, General Resolution No. 9 was
reconsid
ered. The resolution was amended
by striking out "
without specification as
to the chapter name," and
inserting "shall be known by the name of Omeea "

and, in that form, adopted, by following vote :

7

Aye. Theta, Delta, Beta, Sigma, Gamma, Zeta, Lambda, Kappa, Psi, Xi,
Upsilon, Iota, Phi, Pi, Chi, Eta, Tau, Mu, Rho.
JVb. Beta Beta.

Special Resolutions Nos. 3, 4, and 5 were unanimously adopted, without
division, and the Convention then adjourned sine die.

RESOLUTIONS ADOPTED.

GENERAL RESOLUTIONS.

General Resolution No. 1. 

Resolved, That the report of the Treasurer of
the Executive Council be and hereby is approved.
General Resolution No, 2. 

Resolved, That a tax be levied by the Executive
Council upon the chapters at the rate of $1 for each active member on the
rolls on February 1, 1898, for the general purposes of the Fraternity.
General Resolution No. 3. Resolved, That the Committee to evise and
amend, the Constitution, appointed pursuant to General Resolution No. 4 of
1896, he and hereby is authorized to continue until the completion of its work.
General Resolution No. 4. Resolved, That the Executive Council be and
hereby is authorized to employ a Registrar, who shall hold office during the
pleasure of the Council; upon whom may be devolved, subject to the super
vision of the Council, the entire charge of the rolls, reports and other statisti
cal information filed by the chapters with the Council.
General Resolution No. 5. Resolved, That the publication of a general

catalogue of the Fraternity in 1900 be and is hereby authorized, subject to the
approval by the Convention of 1898 of estimates of cost, proposed form, and
other details to be submitted by the Executive Council.
General Resolution No. ^.Resolved, That the Council be and hereby is
authorized to cause the remaining copies of tbe Insignia to be suitably bound.
General Resolution No. 7. Resolved, That the Convention endorse and

approve the action taken by the Council pursuant to General Resolution No.
11 of 1896.
General Resolution No. 8. Resolved, That the applications for the estab-

Ushment of a chapter at St. Stephen's College, Annandale, N. Y., be and are
hereby denied.
General Resolution No. 9. Resolved, That the application for the establish
ment of a chapter, which shall be known by the name of Omega, at the
University of Chicago be granted, and that the action upon the question be
immediately taken by the several chapters of the Fraternity.
General Resolution No. 10. Resolved, That the Executive Council be em

powered to select the chapter with which the sixty-flfth annual convention is
to be held, and that they notify the chapter prior to January 1, 1898.

8

General Resolution No. 11. Resolved, That the standard pin recommended
by the Council be adopted, and that the Council choose an authorized Frater
nity jeweler and notify the chapters of their choice, and that they investigate
the question of the place of wearing the pin, and report further on that ques
tion at the next convention.
General Resolution No.l2. Whereas, On or about the 31st day of .January,
1896, certain graduate members of the Omega Chapter of the Psi Upsilon
Fraternity, viz : Richard B. Twiss, '75; Augustus G. Anderson, '86; Newton
C. Wheeler, '73 ; Thomas C. Roney, '78; James P. Gardner, '81; Charles R.
Calkins, '71; C.T. Otis, '74; C. W. Nicholes, '75 ; H. B. Mitchell, '76 ; C.
R. Dean, '77 ; W. H. Hopkins. '79 ; D. B. Cheney, '80 ; J. C. Hopkins, '81 ;
C. W. Naylor, '81 ; R. F. Harper, '83; P. S. Cheney, '84; H. S. Houston,
'88, and Theodore M. Hammond, '85 ; without any authority or sanction
whatever from the Fraternity, undertook to initiate certain undergraduates
of the University of Chicago into memberbership in the Fraternity, all of the
said undergraduates being members of the so-called Omega Club, which had
on three different occasions applied to the chapters of the Fraternity for a

charter as a chapter of the Fraternity, which application had in each in
stance been denied ; and
WMreas, The Convention of 1896, after hearing the said Richard B.
Twiss on behalf of the said graduate members of the Omega Chapter, did by
general resolution, duly passed, declare the said proceedings of January 31,
1896, to be in violation of the laws of the Fraternity and null and void; and
Whereas, The said Richard B. Twiss, in a public address to the Convention
of 1896, did state that he had, after due deliberation and careful consideration,
advised, aided and prosecuted the said proceedings of January 31, 1896, and
under like circumstances would again pursue the same course and had no
apology or excuse to make for so doing; and
Whereas, The Convention of 1896, by General Resolution No. 11, provided
for the appointment of a Special Committee to which should be submitted
for decision all questions at issue between the said graduate members of the
Omega Chapter and the Fraternity ; and
Whereas, The said Richard B. Twiss on behalf of himself and the said
graduate members of the Omega Chapter, has refused to take any part in any
proceedings or hearing by such Special Committee, pursuant to said General
Resolution No. 11 of 1896; now, therefore, be it
Resolved, That the said R. B. Twiss, A. G. Anderson, N. C. Wheeler T.
C. Roney, J. P. Gardner, C. R. Calkins, C. T. Otis, C. W.
Nicholes, h! B.
Mitchell, C. R. Dean, W. H. Hopkins, D. B. Cheney, J. C. Hopkins C. W.
Naylor, R. F. Harper, F. 8. Cheney, H. S. Houston and T.,M. Hammond be
and hereby are declared guilty of conduct
unworthy of members of the
Fraternity, and prejudicial to its reputation, good order and welfare, and they

9

are hereby suspended from the Fraternity for the period of two years from
the date of the adoption of this resolution.

SPECIAL RESOLUTIONS.

Special Resolution No. 1. 

Resolved, That in the opinion of this Convention
further applications for the establishment of a chapter at St. Stephen's Col

lege, Annandale, N. Y., will be futile.
Special Resolution No. 2. Resolved, That the Convention records its grate

ful appreciation of the service and example of Benjamin H. Bayliss (A '65),
for fourteen years a member of the Executive Council, and its profound sense
of the loss sustained by the Fraternity in his death. We cherish his memorj'
as that of a brother
exemplifying high and unselfish attainment in the spirit
and the principles of Psi Upsilon.
Resolved, That the Executive Council is requested to transmit to the family
of Mr. Bayliss a copy of the foregoing minute.
Special Resolution No. 3. Resolved, That the Convention extends its

thanks to the President and Recorders.

Special Resolution No. 4.
Resolved, That the Convention expresses its

thanks for the admirable arrangements, and its affectionate
Convention
appreciation of the good-fellowship and generous hospitality of the brothers
of the Xi.
Special Resolution No. 5. Resolved, That the convention records its

obligations to Bros. Charles F. Johnson {B '57), orator ; John Kendrick Bangs
{A '83), poet, and George 8. Coleman (t* '76), president of the public literary
exercises.

10

(APPENDIX A.)
THE COMMUNICATION OF THE EXECUTIVE COUNCIL TO
THE CONVENTION OF 1897.

I. Membership. The active membership of the Fraternity on February
1, 1897, according to the annual reports, was 507, an increase of five over the
membership reported in 1896.
II. Constitutional Revision. The committee appointed under Gen
eral Resolution No. 4, of 1896, to revise the Constitution, has not completed
its labors.

III. Insignia. The Council recommends that the greater portion, if not
all, of the remaining copies of the Insignia of Psi Upsilon be bound in cloth
of the Fraternity colors, bearing proper devices, at a cost of about thirty
cents per copy, to be paid out of the General Fund.

IV. List and Register. The Membership List distributed to the Chap
ters in May, 1896, proved to be a matter of so much difficulty in compilation and

publication that the Council has deemed it unwise to make a second issue.
The Council urges upon the Convention the necessity for a permanent, paid
Registrar, upon whom, subject to the supervision of the Council, shall be de
volved the entire charge of rolls, reports and other statistical information of
the Chapters as required for the prompt and inteUigent administration of
Fraternity affairs and the preservation of the Fraternity records.
V. Catalogue. Ten years have passed since the issue of the last Fra

ternity catalogue. Three chapters and ten classes are now wholly uncatalogued,
and the Convention may well consider the publication of a new
catalogue in
1900, the initial step toward which should be taken now, if at all, to the end
that the work may proceed upon fully matured and
carefully studied plans,
with the greatest economy of labor and expense consistent with creditable and
satisfactory results.
VI. Finances. The Fraternity treasury continues to be in a
satisfactory
condition. A renewal of the tax of $1 per active member for the
ensuing year,
to be added to the General Fund, is recommended for the reasons
stated in the
Communication of 1896.
VII. In Memoriam. The Council reports the death, on June 31
1896 of
Joseph W. Harper {A '48), a trustee of Columbia University ; on
February
10, 1897, of William H. Boughton (// '58), author of some of the most
popular
Fraternity songs, and on April 17, 1897, of Henry D. Hyde {F '61), a trustee of
Amherst College. Benjamin H. Bayliss {A
'65), for fourteen years a member
of the Council, died on March 7, 1897. Each of these brothers served and

11

honored the Fraternity, and the Council commends to the chapters emulation
of their virtues and the perpetuation of their memory. The members of the
Council have presented to the Psi Upsilon Club in New York a portrait of
Brother Bayliss, a duplicate of that presented by Lieut. -Gov. Timothy L.
Woodruff (i? '78) to the Memorial Presbyterian Sunday-school of Brooklyn,
of which Mr. Bayliss was for twenty-five years the superintendent.

Vlll. Council Vacanct. The vacancy in the Council, caused by the
death of Brother Bayliss, was filled on March 13, 1897, as prescribed by the

Constitution, by the election of Brother George 8. Coleman (3 '16).

IX. Petitions. The third petition from active and retired members of
the Kappa Gamma Chi Society of St. Stephen's College, Annandale, N. Y.,
is herewith transmitted to the Convention.

X. Universitt op Chicago. In conformity with General Resolution No.
10, of 1896, the Council on June 33, 1896, transmitted to President Harper, of
the University of Chicago, a certified copy of General Resolutions Nos. 8 and
9 of 1896, declaring invalid the proceedings taken on January 31, 1896, to
initiate into the Omega Chapter certain undergraduates of the University.
The undergraduate members of the Omega Club, having been informed of
the illegality of their proceedings, in the autumn of 1896 formally abandoned
their claims to membership in the Fraternity, and subsequently presented a
new petition for admission, the original of which is herewith filed. After
careful personal inquiries and investigation at Chicago by members of the
Council, the Council unanimously approved the petition and submitted it to
the chapters in February, 1897. Fifteen chapters voted in favor of granting
it, viz : Theta, Delta, Sigma, Zeta, Gamma. Lambda, Kappa, Psi, Xi, Pi, Chi,
Beta Beta, Tau, Mu, Rho ; the Iota first voted unanimously in favor, but
afterwards reconsidered and voted unanimously in the negative ; the Phi and
Eta voted in the negative ; the Upsilon suspended action ; the Beta has not
reported. The petition was, therefore, denied. A new petition has been pre
sented, and is herewith submitted to the Convention, with the unanimous
recommendation of the Council.

XI. The Omega. On June 35, 1896. at Chicago, the Council, through
Bro. Bayliss, delivered to Bro. Richard B. Twiss, as the representative of the
<)mega, a stipulation in accordance with the terms of General Resolution No.
11, 1896, providing for the appointment of a Special Committee ; also, that the
graduate members of the Omega would abide by the decision of the Special
Committee, and that meanwhile and until the report of the Committee should
be acted upon by the Convention of 1897, neither the graduate members of
the Omega Chapter nor their organization would attempt to exercise any of

12

the functions of a chapter. On November 5, 1896, Bro. Twiss, for himself
and his associates, notified the Council that they declined to make the stipula
tion required by the Convention of 1897. The stipulation as proposed, and
all correspondence relating thereto, are herewith submitted.

Respectfully submitted,
Herbert L. Bridgman,
Francis S. Bangs,
William M. Kingslet,
Frank L. Hall,
George S. Coleman.
May 6, 1897

(APPENDIX D.)

NOTICE TO THE PRESIDENT OF CHICAGO UNIVERSITY.

New York, June 38, 1896.

To William R. Harper, D.D., President of the University of Chicago, Chicago,
III. :

Dear Sir : Pursuant to the instructions of the Conventionof the Psi
Upsilon Fraternity, held at Ann Arbor, Michigan, on May 7 and 8, 1896, 1 beg
to inform you of the following resolutions, adopted by the Convention, viz. :

General Resolution No. 8. Resolved, That the proceedings taken at Chicago
on January 31. 1896, or other date, purporting in the name of the Omega
Chapter of Psi Upsilon, or otherwise, to initiate into the PsiUpsilon Fraternity
Messrs. Harry W. Stone, Horace R. Dougherty, Raymond W. Stevens, Louis
Wolf, Jr., Ralph H. Johnson, Oswald J. Arnold, Philip Rand, William 8.
Bond, Robert W. Tooker, Moses D. Mclntyre, Arthur Henning, B. B. Smith,
D. A. Kennedy and William E, Goodfellow, or any other undergraduate of
the University of Chicago, were and are in violation of the laws of the Frater
nity, and null and void.
General Resolution No. 9. 

Resolved. That the organization claiming to be
the Omega Chapter of the Psi Upsilon Fraternity, at the University of Chicago,
has no valid existence under the laws of the Psi Upsilon Fraternity.

General Resolution No. 10. Resolved, That the Executive Council be and

is hereby directed to transmit copies of General Resolutions Nos. 8 and 9 to
the proper authorities of the University of Chicago.

Respectfully yours,
F. 8. Bangs,
Se'cretary of the Executive Council of the Psi Upsilon Fraternity.
[Seal of the Fraternity.]

CHICAGO PETITION SUBMITTED TO THE
CHAPTERS,
FEBRUARY 30, 1897.

To the Psi Upsilon Fraternity.
Gentlemen : Your petitioners, undergraduates of the University of
Chicago, relying upon representations made by certain graduate members of
the Omega Chapter of the Psi Upsilon Fraternity, went
through a form of
initiation in January last, purporting to initiate us into the Psi
Upsilon Fra
ternity. We were told that there were certain irregularities in the proceedinffs
which were, however, simply matters of form, and that the initiation
would
he ratified by the convention of the Fraternity.
We have no intention of defying the Fraternity, and do not desire to con
sider ourselves members of the Fraternity, unless initiated in a
legal way
^'and
with the consent of the chapters.

17

Since we have been informed that our initiation was regarded by the
Fraternity as illegal, we have, as a sign of our good faith in the matter, ceased
to clairn the privileges of members, and we now respectfully petition the
Fraternity to take such measures as shall render us legal members of the
Fraternity, by granting a charter to your petitioners under some chapter name
not previously borne by any chapter, by
ordering a new initiation, and taking
sucn other measures as are prescribed
by the Constitution of the Fraternity,
in order that the Fraternity may be represented in a fitting manner in this

St. Stephen's College,
Annandale-on-Hudbon, April, 1897.
To the Executive Council and Chapters of the Psi Upsilon Fraternity :
Gentlemen : The undersigned, representing the active and past members
of the Kappa Gamma Chi of St. Stephen's College, Annandale-on-Hudson,
N. Y., do hereby make this, our third, application for a charter of Psi Upsilon.
In support of our petition, we again call the attention of Psi Upsilon to the
fact that our Fraternity has existed as a
strictly secret and local organization
since 1868.
It has always maintained a high tone and standard, drawing its members
from among the best men in the college. It has always sought a small mem
bership, thus securing a choice of the men. The active membership to-day
is fourteen.
Meetings are held weekly, with formal literary exercises, and in addition
there are frequent gatherings of a distinctly social nature.
It is a most representative Fraternity, both in scholarship and undergradu
ate affairs. The building fund for a new chapter house is in a prosperous con
dition, and the final plans for the building will be submitted at the annual re
union in June.
With this petition we present additional reasons why a chapter of Psi Up
silon should be established in St. Stephen's, and we respectfully recall the
long list of Psi Upsilon alumni, who endorsed our first application.
During the past year the Fraternity has maintained a vigorous existence,
and holds steadfastly to its purpose to press forward to a high ideal of fra
ternity life and work.
In this spirit, we again respectfully apply to you for a charter of Psi
Upsilon. Respectfully yours,
A. Randolph B. Hegeman,
Francis C. Steinmetz,

St. Stephen's a college of liberal arts, not a technical school.
We desire especially to correct the impression that St. Stephen's College
is a technical school. This is an error that has arisen by reason of the fact
that so many of the alumni of St. Stephen's take a theological course after
graduating from the college.
A technical school is one which gives a course preparatory to a particular
profession and is permitted to grant only such professional degrees as are pro
vided for its curriculum.
While St. Stephen's by its charter can grant any degree whatever, no
theology is studied at St. Stephen's. The students are taking the usual course
in aits preparatory to any profession, and on receiving his degree of B. A.
from St. Stephen's a man is prepared to enter on the study of law, medicine,
theology, civic.s, etc., as he elects, but he has had no technical instruction in
any one of these professions. St. Stephen's has alumni who are now lawyers,
physicians, clergymen, business men, brokers, journalists, actors, etc., and
hence it is in every way acollege of the liberal arts. St. Stephen's stands in
the same class with Trinity and Kenyon. All three are "church" colleges,
i.e., under the government of ecclesiastical authority, and offering such spe
cial privileges as will attract those men who expect ultimately to enter the
ministry of the church, but St. Stephen's, like all other colleges, leaves the
technical instruction for the professional school. The late Rev. Charles P.
Hoffman, D.D., of New York City, recognized the work of the college by
frequent benefactions, amounting in all to nearly $300,000.
8t. Stephen's, with its distinctively collegiate character, offers a field
especially fitted for fraternity fife, and has every indication of a great future.
In view of these facts. Kappa Gamma Chi urges again the establishment of a
chapter of Psi Upsilon at this time, when the field is almost clear, Sigma
Alpha Epsilon alone having entered the college. It will be the fraternity that
enters now that will accomplish the best and most permanent results.
Further information concerning St. Stephen's, or the Kappa Gamma Chi
will be furnished on application to Mr. Jos. P. Gilson, Annandale-on-
Hudson, N. Y., or the Rev. A. R. B. Hegeman, 105 Ten Broeck street '
Albany, N. Y.
